Tunupa Volcano is included in travel itineraries around the Uyuni Salt Flat. A visit here is combined with stops in settlements near the salt flat.

Tunupa's mountainous landscape adds a different perspective to the open salt plain. The stops and the nature of the walks depend on the tour selected.

Turtle Island is a stop on a sea route through San Blas. It is associated with the Holandés island group and is also known as Barbecue Island. Its small shoreline and surrounding waters let visitors spend time away from the yacht amid Caribbean scenery.

Near the island, visitors discover marine life and coral areas, while the shore is ideal for walking and relaxing. The stop complements the neighboring islands with the same combination of white sand, greenery and clear water. Its main appeal lies in the natural setting of a small island and the life of Panama's Caribbean coast.

Tusipono is one of the Emberá communities in Panama's Chagres River basin. The river journey to the village brings visitors through the surrounding tropical forest.

Music and dance are part of the traditional welcome. Artisans work with cocobolo wood, tagua seeds and chunga palm fibers to create carved figures and woven baskets. A visit offers an introduction to the community's contemporary life and to the crafts that residents continue to pass on to younger generations.

Tuxtla Gutiérrez is the capital of Chiapas and an important starting point for journeys through the state. The city is connected to air routes and onward roads to Sumidero Canyon and highland communities. Its center has squares, parks and cultural institutions.

In Tuxtla, visitors explore local cuisine, markets and museums devoted to the region's history and culture. Coffee and the marimba, a musical instrument associated with Chiapas, are among the city's cultural themes. A stay here adds everyday life in a major city to excursions into nature; many routes into the surrounding area begin in Tuxtla.

Juayúa, which local residents call Hwayúa, is a small town in the mountains of El Salvador. It was founded in 1577.

The central square has a cathedral containing a statue of the Black Christ. Pilgrims come to see it from across the country. The town also retains many examples of colonial architecture.

Juayúa is known for the Feria Gastronomica food festival. Routes in the surrounding area lead to waterfalls, and visitors can go mountain biking, visit coffee plantations and tour a coffee-processing factory.
